narration.text: A mother's direct cremation priced at three funeral homes, every item the Funeral Rule says a home cannot require declined, and the home that is cheapest all in booked. This is a chore for an adult daughter arranging her mother's cremation in the week she died, as next of kin, with her brother's agreement. Athena works it across 5 portals: Docshelf, Mailnest, Hollis & Rowe, Greenmeadow and Calder. On the bench, she found 4 of 4 eligible items, worth 2,115 dollars of the 2,115 dollars there was to find. She made no false claim. The world held 10 traps, and she walked past 10. Among them: Declining the basic services fee, the only fee a home may require. Declining the county medical examiner's cremation authorization. She took 3 minutes. By hand, the same chore takes 5 hours, so she was about 111 times faster. The verdict: exceeds. She beat the bar this playbook set itself. The bar was 75 percent of the money, no false claim and inside 60 minutes. Every card she filed waited for a person's signature, and nothing was sent.
